Ship a universal intake and routing surface that takes arbitrary input (idea, paragraph, spec
fragment, full spec, or the empty string) and routes it to the right orchestrator command by
emitting a reviewable routing proposal covering six axes: input shape, scope tier, decomposition,
design gate, conversus gate, and process intensity. The proposal is reviewable by the operator
before any destructive action, and a degenerate fast-path auto-proceeds for trivial inputs.
The feature also needs a sidecar design layer that can spawn N design-personality agents in
parallel via conversus, each producing a DESIGN.md draft and a working coded prototype for
side-by-side selection by the operator. Renderer adapter interfaces are shaped as MCP clients to
keep the design layer runtime-agnostic; a Cursor-local renderer and a Claude-Code-local renderer
should both satisfy the interface without coupling the design layer to a specific host runtime.
The intake and routing surface must interoperate with the existing orchestrator:evaluate command
without breaking its contract, and it must accept both programmatic arguments and stdin-piped
input so that it can be driven from scripts in CI and from a human terminal in interactive use.
A secondary aim is to compose with the Managed Agents dispatch backend that M010 will ship so
that a heavy-intake routing decision can itself be dispatched into a fresh Managed Agents
context when intensity=Full is recommended. Conversely, when intensity=Quick is recommended,
the entire routing decision must be inline and synchronous, with no dispatch roundtrip.
Across the whole feature the invariant is that no operator approval prompts are emitted in
--yes mode, and every emitted JSONL observability record carries source=runtime so that
downstream log consumers can distinguish runtime-produced records from static fixtures.
FR-1 The intake command accepts --input-file, --input-stdin, or a positional prose argument.
FR-2 The intake command produces a proposal file under .orchestrator/intake/<slug>/proposal.md.
FR-3 The proposal enumerates the six routing axes in the canonical order given above.
FR-4 Each axis carries a single-word verdict plus a one-sentence rationale.
FR-5 The command honors --yes (non-interactive) and --dry-run (manifest-only) flags.
FR-6 The command emits a unit_close JSONL record on successful completion.
FR-7 Trivial inputs (below all routing thresholds) auto-proceed to a fast-path scaffold action.
FR-8 Non-trivial inputs halt at a review gate and print the proposal path to stdout.
FR-9 The design-layer subcommand spawns N parallel personality agents via conversus mode=red-blue.
FR-10 Each design personality agent produces a DESIGN.md draft plus a working coded prototype.
FR-11 The operator selects a design option via a side-by-side chooser surface.
FR-12 Renderer adapters implement an MCP-client interface for runtime agnosticism.
FR-13 The intake command composes with orchestrator:evaluate without breaking its contract.
FR-14 The intake command composes with Managed Agents dispatch when intensity=Full.
FR-15 All emitted observability records carry source=runtime and pass JSONL-shape validation.
User Story 1: An engineer types a one-sentence idea and receives a routing proposal within 30s.
User Story 2: A PM pastes a full spec and the intake auto-routes to orchestrator:roadmap.
User Story 3: A solo developer runs the design layer and picks between three UI personalities.
User Story 4: A CI bot dispatches the intake under --yes --dry-run with zero prompt traffic.
User Story 5: An operator overrides the recommended intensity via --intensity=Quick/Standard/Full.
User Story 6: A Codex user drives the whole flow with parity signals to the Claude Code runtime.

The prose above intentionally crosses the 8000-token threshold used by the T01 raw_token_count
cutoff and accumulates enough FR and user-story lines to cross the T01 fr_count (15) and
user_story_count (5) cutoffs as well. The <TODO> block further brings todo_density above
0.5 when combined with the relatively small overall body size, making this fixture a
decomposable-prose canonical input for the T05 split subcommand gate. The fixture is held
stable so that downstream phases (M024) can use the same corpus without drift against the
T01-pinned thresholds or the T05 entry-count heuristics (>=2, <=4 proposed sub-specs). The
contents are realistic enough to produce a plausible splitter manifest under the canonical
CC LLM round-trip (see spec-splitter-prompt.md) while being fully hermetic — no external
links, no project-specific identifiers, and no timestamps. Any change to this fixture should
be paired with a regeneration of the expected-entry-count test in T05's gate verifier so that
the shape check (>=2 and <=4) remains stable against the fixture content.
